maria: Anyone else hitting mypy/pyright errors from the Python SDK autogen models during the sampleapp onboarding? Repro below, looks like a kw-only list field + None interaction.

maria: Repro (really minimal):
```py
from sampleapp import Client, GeneratedModel

c = Client()
m = GeneratedModel(id=\"x\", tags=None)
# mypy: error: Argument 2 to \"GeneratedModel\" has incompatible type \"None\"; expected \"List[str]\"\n```

maria: The generator emits something like:
```py
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Optional

@dataclass
class GeneratedModel:
    id: str
    tags: Optional[List[str]] = None  # kw_only
```

jonathan: Can you paste the exact mypy/pyright output? Is this when calling the constructor or when assigning later?

maria: It's at call site (constructor). mypy complains because the dataclass init signature is inferred as (id: str, tags: List[str]) even though default is None — maybe due to kw_only generation. Output snippet: 
```
example.py:10: error: Argument 1 to \"GeneratedModel\" has incompatible type \"None\"; expected \"List[str]\"  [arg-type]\n```

kai: Huh. Two quick angles: 1) make the generated type List[str] with default_factory=list (no Optional) so mypy always sees a List and callers passing None will be a runtime error (or you can normalize in __post_init__). 2) Keep Optional[List[str]] but make the generated __init__ signature accept Optional[List[str]] explicitly (mypy-friendly) and convert None -> [] inside the model for runtime.

maria: I'd prefer preserving None semantics for backwards compatibility (None meaning \"unset\" vs empty list). But we also want the SDK to be mypy/pyright-friendly for users following static typing.

jonathan: Pragmatic compromise: generate the public __init__ with Optional[List[str]] (so callers can pass None and mypy is happy), and add a post-init normalization that leaves internal representation as None if the model schema says \"nullable\", otherwise sets []. That keeps typing accurate and runtime correct.

kai: Example generator template change:
```py
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import List, Optional

@dataclass
class GeneratedModel:
    id: str
    tags: Optional[List[str]] = None

    def __post_init__(self):
        # normalize for runtime but keep type hint Optional[List[str]] for callers
        if getattr(self, 'tags', None) is None:
            # if API schema says default -> [], convert here, otherwise keep None
            self.tags = []  # or leave None depending on property.nullable
```

maria: That looks good. Would mypy complain about assigning [] to Optional[List[str]]? No, that assignment is allowed since [] is a List[str], subtype of Optional[List[str]].

jonathan: Right. Also we should update the typing stubs we ship with the SDK (and the generated __init__ signature) so pyright sees Optional on the parameter. Some users reported pyright inferring a narrower signature from runtime introspection which causes noise in editors.

maria: Another related issue: async client overloads — pyright sometimes flags the sync client methods returning Union[SyncResult, Awaitable[SyncResult]] because of our unified Client that can return coroutine when used in async context. Folks suggested separate AsyncClient to avoid union-y returns.

kai: Yep, we should avoid ambiguous return types. We should either provide explicit overloads in the stubs or split into Client / AsyncClient classes. Overloads are smaller change.

maria: Action items: 1) jonathan will open a generator PR to make constructor params Optional where schema allows null and add explicit __post_init__ normalization. 2) kai will draft a second PR to add typing-only overloads for async methods (so mypy/pyright see correct return types). 3) I'll add a small sampleapp test covering mypy/pyright checks in CI and a repro snippet in the devex repo.

jonathan: I'll CC @dev-bot on the PR so CI runs the typing checks.

dev-bot: CI started for branch \"maria/typing-kwlist-fix\" — running mypy + pyright + unit tests. (I'll post results in this thread.) :robot_face:

maria: thanks! if anyone wants to take the list-default-vs-none UX debate, ping me — would like a short doc describing recommended semantics for generated arrays.

jonathan: Will do.
